c.tagline: Home of the world's first Pilsner, with a walkable old town and UNESCO-listed underground tunnels.

taxi.fareNote: Use official taxi stands or apps (Bolt, Liftago); street-hailed cabs sometimes overcharge tourists.

emergency.note: General EU emergency number 112 also works and often has English-speaking operators.

hood_desc: The compact historic core centered on Republic Square, packed with Gothic and Renaissance facades, the cathedral, and the entrance to the underground tunnel network. Most sights, restaurants, and hotels are within a short walk here.
Home to the Pilsner Urquell brewery complex and its popular tours and beer spa; a mix of industrial heritage sites and casual pubs just east of the Old Town.
A green, residential district north of downtown built around the Bolevec fishponds, popular for walking, swimming, and cycling away from the tourist crowds.
A quiet southwestern district known for the city zoo and botanical garden, plus leafy suburban streets and family housing.
A mixed residential-commercial district just southeast of downtown with local shops, the historic Great Synagogue, and everyday Czech neighborhood life.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.pay: Contactless card tap, PMDP mobile app, or paper tickets from machines/kiosks
transit.note: Dense tram and trolleybus network (PMDP) covers the whole city; the Old Town itself is easily walkable.

train: Direct trains to Prague (~1.5hr) and Munich via České dráhy
bus: FlixBus and RegioJet coaches to Prague and other cities

tip.r: Round up or add 5-10% at sit-down restaurants; not expected for taxis, cafes, or takeaway.

landmarks: Pilsner Urquell Brewery
Birthplace of golden lager in 1842, its cellar tour ends with unfiltered Pilsner poured straight from oak barrels in cool sandstone tunnels.
Cathedral of St. Bartholomew
Its 102-meter Gothic spire, the tallest church tower in Czechia, rewards climbers with sweeping panoramas over Republic Square's Renaissance facades.
Republic Square (Namesti Republiky)
One of Europe's largest medieval squares mixes modern gilded fountains, a baroque plague column and colorful burgher houses around the cathedral.
Great Synagogue
The second-largest synagogue in Europe, a Moorish-Romanesque marvel of 1893 with onion-domed twin towers, now hosts concerts and exhibitions after painstaking restoration.
Pilsen Historical Underground
Fourteen kilometers of medieval cellars, wells and passageways burrow beneath the old town, revealing how citizens brewed, stored and sheltered below ground.
Brewery Museum
Set in an original medieval malt house, it traces beer-making from ancient Mesopotamia to the lager revolution that made Pilsen world-famous.
Renaissance Town Hall
This Italian-designed palazzo of 1558, its facade covered in elaborate sgraffito decoration, dominates Republic Square beside the gilded plague column.
Patton Memorial Pilsen
This heartfelt museum honors the US Third Army's liberation of Pilsen in May 1945, a story suppressed during four decades of communism.
Techmania Science Center
A hands-on science playground in a former Skoda factory hall, its interactive exhibits and 3D planetarium make physics irresistible for families.
Puppet Museum
Celebrating the cherished Czech marionette tradition, this playful museum lets visitors pull the strings of Spejbl and Hurvinek, Pilsen's beloved puppet duo.

train.note: Plzeň is on the main line from Prague to Bavaria, so the Munich trains via Domažlice and Schwandorf call here - about 3h15 to Munich, with an electrification upgrade steadily improving journey times. Prague is 90 minutes away with frequent services. The station is a 15-minute walk from the square. Book ČD tickets online for the cheaper advance fares.

bus.note: Coaches use the CAN bus terminal near the station. FlixBus and RegioJet run direct to Munich in about 3h30 and to Nuremberg, which is competitive with the train. Domestically, buses to Prague are frequent and take about an hour. Carry your passport or EU ID card.

ferry.note: Czechia is landlocked and Plzeň's four small rivers are not navigable, so there are no ferries of any kind.
